formal: Department of Electrical, Computer and Biomedical Engineering
summary: The Department of Electrical, Computer and Biomedical Engineering (DIII) is a leading academic unit dedicated to advancing scientific and technological progress in engineering. Its mission encompasses fostering education, driving innovation, and facilitating technology transfer across various engineering disciplines. The Department focuses on addressing contemporary challenges and opportunities in fields such as telecommunications, automotive, artificial intelligence, data science, energy, high-performance computing, imaging, multimedia, IoT, embedded systems, remote sensing, life science, bioengineering, mechatronics, microelectronics, photonics, numerical modeling, and industrial automation.
description:
The Department of Electrical, Computer and Biomedical Engineering (DIII) is a dynamic research and educational institution committed to excellence in the broad field of engineering. The Department plays a crucial role in the scientific, technological, and socio-economic development of modern society by serving as a hub for advanced training, groundbreaking innovation, and effective technology transfer. Its comprehensive approach to engineering education and research prepares future generations of engineers and scientists to tackle complex global challenges.

The Department's research activities span a wide array of cutting-edge areas, reflecting the interdisciplinary nature of contemporary engineering. Key research lines include the development of advanced 5G and telecommunications systems, innovative solutions in automotive engineering, and the application of artificial intelligence and data science for complex problem-solving. Furthermore, the Department is actively involved in research concerning sustainable energy solutions, high-performance computing architectures, and advanced imaging and multimedia processing techniques.

Specialized research also extends to the Internet of Things (IoT), embedded systems, and remote sensing for diverse applications. The Department contributes significantly to life science and bioengineering through technological advancements, and explores the integration of mechanical, electrical, and computer engineering in mechatronics. Research in microelectronics and photonics focuses on developing next-generation devices, while numerical modeling for engineering science provides critical tools for analysis and design. Finally, the Department is at the forefront of robotics and industrial automation, developing intelligent systems for various industrial and service sectors.
